title: Horizon and Signal
premise: Sable Almeida has spent eleven years alone in the Meridian Seed Vault, tending cryopods and recording logs for a colony that stopped answering. When a ghost ship called the Vesper docks with a manifest bearing his own dead sister's name, Sable learns the vault's reactor is failing and only half the sleepers can be revived before it dies. The ship's crew—strangers who claim to be rescuers—are actually scavengers harvesting colonists for organs on the black market, and the name on the manifest belongs to one of them wearing a stolen identity. Sable must choose which pods to wake: the engineers and children who could rebuild, or the strangers whose memories hold proof of what happened to Earth. In the end he wakes neither faction whole but a mixed handful of survivors, destroys the Vesper's harvest cargo, and launches the vault's seed archive toward a distant colony while staying behind to die with the station—until the final chapter reveals his own pod was among those launched, his memory of choosing sacrifice itself a recorded log.
about_author: Odile Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things running after everyone else has gone home.

chapters.title: The Long Inventory
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He walks the vault's endless corridors checking seed drawers and pod vitals, narrating his daily ritual to a recorder no one hears. Establishes his loneliness, competence, and the eleven-year silence from Earth. Emotional beat: tender routine masking grief.

chapters.title: Log 4,012
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He records an anniversary message to the colony council, admitting for the first time that he doesn't believe anyone will ever play it back. A minor power fluctuation hints at the reactor's decay. Emotional beat: hope curdling into ritual.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. An automated docking alert—the first in years—announces the Vesper, a ship class decommissioned before the colony fell silent. Its manifest lists 'Iris Almeida,' his sister, dead twelve years. Emotional beat: shock cracking open the numbness.

chapters.title: Ghosts Docking
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He watches the ship land through frost-fogged glass, torn between terror and desperate hope that Iris somehow survived. He arms himself with a maintenance tool and goes to meet them. Emotional beat: trembling anticipation.

chapters.title: Four Strangers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Vesper's crew arrives: Captain Reyes, medic Okafor, engineer Tomaš, and a quiet young woman calling herself Iris Almeida—who looks nothing like his sister. They claim to be a rescue mission. Emotional beat: hope deferred, suspicion kindled.

chapters.title: The Woman Called Iris
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins alternating with the impostor 'Iris' (real name Wren). Wren studies Sable, guilt-ridden about using a dead girl's name, while Sable tests her with childhood memories she cannot answer. Emotional beat: two liars circling each other.

chapters.title: Reactor Mathematics
chapters.summary: Tomaš's POV. He privately confirms the vault reactor will fail within months and reports to Reyes that only half the pods can be sustained—a fact they conceal from Sable. Introduces the crew's hidden agenda. Emotional beat: cold calculation.

chapters.title: Tea with a Stranger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He shares his hoarded real tea with Wren, and she almost confesses her deception but instead asks about the sleepers. He describes them like family—because they are. Emotional beat: unexpected intimacy.

chapters.title: The Children's Wing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She tours the pod bays and sees forty sleeping children; her scavenger resolve wavers. Reyes reminds her of the debt she owes and the life waiting if she completes the job. Emotional beat: conscience versus coercion.

chapters.title: What Earth Forgot
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He shows the crew the vault's true purpose: not just seeds but cultural archives, the colony's entire memory. Reyes's interest sharpens in a way Sable can't read. Emotional beat: pride shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: Static from the Deep
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. While repairing the antenna he intercepts a fragmentary distress call matching the Vesper's registry—an old mayday from a ship that supposedly never flew. Emotional beat: dread taking shape.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Her medical logs reveal the truth obliquely: sedatives stockpiled, surgical supplies, 'harvest candidates' coded as rescue priorities. She justifies it as triage. Emotional beat: complicity dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The First Lie Cracks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren slips and references a detail of Iris's death that was never public. Sable says nothing, but begins secretly reviewing docking records. Emotional beat: quiet betrayal.

chapters.title: Countdown Discovered
chapters.summary: Tomaš's POV. Tomaš, increasingly sympathetic to Sable, leaves the reactor report where the caretaker will find it. The math is brutal: power for roughly half the pods, and the clock is running. Emotional beat: guilt becoming action.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Confronted with the numbers, Sable faces the choice the blurb promised—which sleepers wake. He begins building criteria and hates every one of them. Emotional beat: the weight of arithmetic over lives.

chapters.title: Reyes Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The captain offers Sable passage off the vault in exchange for full access to the archives and 'assistance with triage.' Sable recognizes the word's wrongness. Emotional beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Memories for Sale
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapters begin: Wren's childhood in the orbital slums, how she bought a dead girl's identity to escape them. Her memory theme deepens—she chose to forget herself. Emotional beat: sympathy for the thief.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers someone accessed the cultural archives and copied files on colony defense systems. The 'rescuers' wanted more than passengers. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable/Wren. Both sneak through the vault at night on separate investigations and collide in the seed corridors. Forced into an uneasy alliance by mutual suspicion of Reyes. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing kinship.

chapters.title: What Happened to Iris
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Records show Iris died aboard a ship registered to Reyes's family company—one of the first 'harvests.' The manifest name wasn't random; it was a message or a taunt. Emotional beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Tomaš's Choice
chapters.summary: Tomaš's POV. Ordered to sabotage the vault's external comms, Tomaš fakes it instead, buying Sable time to broadcast a warning beacon. Emotional beat: a coward finding his line.

chapters.title: The Beacon
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The warning goes out—but so does their location. Sable realizes any rescue is months away and the reactor won't wait. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes discovers the betrayal, seals the crew's authority over the ship, and moves up the 'evacuation' schedule. The vault becomes a cage with a countdown. Emotional beat: menace fully revealed.

chapters.title: Seeds and Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the harvest manifests—hundreds of names across years—and finds Iris Almeida among them. She brings the evidence to Sable, finally surrendering the stolen name. Emotional beat: confession as absolution sought.

chapters.title: The Criteria
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable finalizes his list: the children, the engineers, the teachers—not the strong, the necessary. He shows Wren, asking her to help him choose who lives. Emotional beat: shared unbearable weight.

chapters.title: Mutiny in the Bays
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Okafor refuses to sedate the first pod batch; Tomaš sides with her; Reyes isolates them. The crew fractures along the fault line the vault has drawn. Emotional beat: found family forming inside the enemy.

chapters.title: Power Play
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reroutes vault power to lock the harvest bay, gambling the reactor's remaining life against Reyes's patience. The countdown accelerates. Emotional beat: defiance burning fuel.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under sedative haze in the infirmary, Wren recovers the memory she buried: she knew Iris, briefly, in the slums—gave her the idea to run. The name was both theft and memorial. Emotional beat: memory as reckoning.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Airlock Nine
chapters.summary: Sable and Reyes face-to-face. Reyes offers again: walk away rich, let the pods be 'processed.' Sable counters with the archive's self-destruct failsafe. Stalemate. Emotional beat: two survivors negotiating with humanity as currency.

chapters.title: The Reactor Speaks
chapters.summary: Tomaš's POV. Emergency diagnostics: seventy-two hours of power remain, enough to wake one pod batch OR launch the seed archive, not both. The thematic choice crystallizes: save people or save what people made. Emotional beat: the premise's knife turned.

chapters.title: Children First
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable commits: wake the children and essential adults, launch the archive unmanned, stay behind himself. Wren argues fiercely that he must come. He refuses. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen without drama.

chapters.title: Okafor's Atonement
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. She begins the revival sequence, administering counteragents to her own stockpiled sedatives, working through the night. Each waking child is a small repudiation of her ledger. Emotional beat: redemption through labor.

chapters.title: Reyes Retaliates
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Denied his cargo, Reyes attempts to seize the archive module as salvage. Tomaš traps him in the docking ring; Reyes kills him in the struggle. Emotional beat: the cost of conscience made flesh.

chapters.title: Fire in the Corridors
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With Reyes loose and systems failing, Sable lures him into the seed vault's atmospheric control and floods the chamber—an execution he will carry forever. Emotional beat: survival staining the savior.

chapters.title: Launch
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The archive module and a shuttle of twenty-three awakened sleepers depart together. Wren refuses to board until the last second; Sable puts her on the shuttle physically and seals it. Emotional beat: farewell as gift.

chapters.title: The Last Log
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Alone, dying reactor around him, Sable records his final entry—a letter to the children, to Iris, to whoever finds the vault. He chooses to spend his last hours planting a garden in the hydroponics bay. Emotional beat: serenity earned.

chapters.title: Signal Received
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, aboard the fleeing shuttle. The beacon's warning reached a distant outpost; a rescue response is inbound—for the vault, too late, they all know. Wren plays Sable's logs for the waking children. Emotional beat: inheritance of memory.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Years later, the survivors reach the colony world and plant the first seeds from the archive. Wren keeps Sable's recorder running, adding entries. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into continuity.

chapters.title: The Garden Still Grows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Final revelation: among the launched modules was one unmarked pod—Sable's, added by Tomaš before his death, its revival cycle still counting down. Wren stands before it. Emotional beat: stunned, trembling hope.

chapters.title: Wake
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The pod opens. Sable wakes to sunlight, soil, and the sound of children—he remembers choosing to die, and cannot reconcile it with breathing air. Wren tells him: 'You don't get to decide what survives you.' Emotional beat: grace, undeserved and accepted.
